claim: Qwenputer is a stock Qwen 3.5 4B model with a RISC-V CPU embedded in its weights that uses the model's Gated DeltaNet layers as RAM.
quote: It's a stock Qwen 3.5 4B with one addition: a RISC-V CPU embedded within the weights that uses the model's own Gated DeltaNet attention layers as RAM.

claim: The blog post is by Divyansh Agrawal, dated 22 October 2026 (before the digest window).
quote: By Divyansh Agrawal 22 October 2026

claim: The author describes it as experimental.
quote: Qwenputer is very much an experiment, so a few limitations.

claim: Setting gate=1, beta=1 and one-hot keys makes each write overwrite exactly one row and each query read an exact value.
quote: every write we perform will overwrite exactly one row, and every one-hot query can retrieve an exact value.

claim: No training is involved; a compiler sets every weight.
quote: Luckily, there's no training involved: a compiler sets every weight directly.

claim: The CPU is 32-bit RV32IM plus Zba and a bignum unit, occupying 11 layers in front of Qwen's 32.
quote: The CPU is a 32-bit RISC-V core (RV32IM, plus the Zba extension and a small bignum unit for big-number arithmetic), and it takes up 11 layers in front of Qwen's 32.

claim: Author claims it passes official riscv-tests, matches qemu and ran 18 million instructions free-running without error.
quote: it passes the official riscv-tests, its programs match qemu, and it has run 18 million instructions free-running without a single error.

claim: Author reports mul_big accuracy of 97.5% vs 100% with a Python tool and 55% for base Qwen.
quote: mul_big: Qwenputer scores 97.5%, versus 100% with a Python tool and 55% for base Qwen.

claim: Benchmarks used 40 problems per set with greedy decoding.
quote: Greedy decoding, 40 problems per set.

claim: About 230,000 output positions were replayed against a reference machine with zero mismatches.
quote: I replayed about 230,000 of its output positions against a reference machine and found zero mismatches.

claim: Normal text behaviour stays within noise of base Qwen.
quote: its normal text stays within noise of base Qwen (KL 6e-4, against a noise floor of 5e-4).

claim: The experimental filesystem gets changed facts right 90% of the time vs 30% when pasting old chats.
quote: Qwen gets facts that changed between chats right 90% of the time, against 30% when you paste the old chats back in

claim: Checkpoint is 18.8 GB, about double base Qwen, mostly zero padding.
quote: make the checkpoint 18.8 GB, roughly double base Qwen, although most of it is zero padding.

claim: It needs the RvChat driver and does not run with plain generate().
quote: so it doesn't run with a plain generate() call yet.

claim: It is slow: big calculations take seconds; ~3,200 CPU tokens/sec on an L4.
quote: The batched executor I used for the benchmarks runs about 3,200 CPU tokens a second on an L4.

claim: Next steps: a python() tool running MicroPython in the weights, and a faster CPU.
quote: through a python() tool that works the same way calc does. Making the CPU faster is the other big one.

claim: Delta-rule memory is prior work (Schlag et al. 2021); the claimed novelty is exactness inside a production model.
quote: The new thing here is making it exact and addressable, inside a production model, reliably enough to run a whole CPU on it.

claim: Code is MIT; weights Apache-2.0 with Qwen's own weights unchanged.
quote: The code is MIT. The model weights are Apache-2.0

claim: The HF model was created 2026-10-19 and lists Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B as base model.
quote: "createdAt": "2026-10-19T18:51:39.000Z" ... "base_model": "Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B"

claim: The HN post reached 695 points on 2026-10-29.
The author says it is spare-time work.
quote: I just do these during my free time.

claim: Critic says a custom host runtime still loads firmware and skips Qwen's layers, calling the 'no external runtime' claim a little dishonest.
quote: The central claim about “no external runtime” or “not a plugin” feels a little dishonest to me since this doesn’t work without some pretty invasive changes to the inference driver.

claim: Critic questions usefulness of a sub-100% calculator.
quote: I'm sorry but I'm not sure I understand how a calculator that isn't 100% accurate is useful?

claim: Commenter: it refutes the misconception that LLMs are inherently non-deterministic.
quote: It is a great example to refute the common misconception that LLMs are inherently non-deterministic.

claim: Lobsters top comment argues a normal RISC-V emulator would give the same result.
quote: you could get the same result by using a normal RISC-V emulator

claim: Loom (preprint) already ran C programs in a looped transformer with analytically derived weights.
quote: We present Loom, a computer architecture that executes programs compiled from C inside a looped transformer whose weights are derived analytically.

claim: nesformer builds on Qwenputer's compiler to run an NES CPU in Qwen3.5 weights.
quote: It reuses Qwenputer's compiler and its central trick: **the model's Gated DeltaNet state is the machine's memory.**

claim: doomformer computes neural networks inside DOOM maps (not DOOM as a transformer).
quote: Neural networks computed by voodoo dolls inside DOOM maps.
